# Recreation Prompt

Create `Vice Grid: Wanted Streets`, a portrait-first browser-native 3D open-city action sandbox inspired by Grand Theft Auto-style systemic mischief. Preserve a simple free-roam loop with camera-relative joystick movement, enter/exit or summon cars, weapon switching, fist/gun attacks, health-based failure, wanted-star escalation, police pursuit, building collisions, zoom, camera rotation, start and restart. Reinterpret the player as a neon street climber in a satirical city district. Use mobile-readable HUD terms like NERVE and DISPATCH, procedural boulevard asphalt, neon building facades, police siren bars, compact minimap and billboard motifs, and touch-friendly controls. Do not add new win conditions or alter input semantics.
blueprint_markdown:
# Blueprint

## Source truth
The preserved source is a browser-native Three.js 3D open-city sandbox. The player controls a humanoid on foot with a mobile joystick, rotates/zooms the camera, enters nearby cars or summons a car, switches fist/gun weapons, attacks NPCs/cars, loses health from impacts or enemy fire, and reaches a game-over state when health reaches zero. Progress pressure is the wanted/heat star level, which escalates when the player defeats entities and can spawn police cars that pursue the player.

## Protected mechanics
- Camera-relative joystick movement on foot.
- Car acceleration/steering when entered, plus exit via the same interact button.
- Interact button enters nearby car within the existing range or summons a car when no car is close.
- Attack button uses current weapon; switch button toggles fist/gun.
- Building collision, car impact damage, punch proximity, gun line hit checks, health failure, wanted-star escalation/decay, police AI pursuit, zoom slider, camera rotate, start/restart flow.

## Remixed target
`Vice Grid: Wanted Streets` reinterprets the same mechanics as a mobile-first open-city crime-chaos satire: a street climber roams a neon city, calls getaway rides, escalates dispatch heat, and survives police pursuit. Presentation, HUD language, textures, entity styling, and scene atmosphere are transformed; mechanics remain intact.
